pr_title: Explicit parsing object capabilities of FieldMappers
pr_body:
When the subobject property is set to false and we encounter an object 
while parsing we need a way to understand if its FieldMapper is able to 
parse an object. If that's the case we can provide the entire object to 
the FieldMapper otherwise its name becomes the part of the dotted field
name of each internal value (PR for this feature open here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88934).

This has being achieved by adding the `supportsParsingObject()` method 
to the `FieldMapper` class. This method defaults to `false` since the 
majority of FieldMappers do not support parsing objects and is 
overwritten to return `true` by the ones that do support objects.

To test this feature we implemented `testSupportsParsingObject()` in 
`MapperTestCase`. There if the field `supportsParsingObject` we get a 
sample object for testing from `getSampleObjectForDocument`, we 
parse it and make sure that the resulting document is not null.
If otherwise the FieldMapper does not support parsing objects we provide
an empty object for parsing and expect an exception.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/98537

### Description

When the subobject property is set to false and we encounter an object while parsing
we need a way to understand if its fieldMapper is able to parse an object.
If that's the case we can provide the entire object to the FieldMapper otherwise its
name becomes the  part of the dotted field name of each internal value.

This feature will be used for https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88934
